verdict.rationale: Cooley publishes a dedicated page for Cooley AI, described as a firm-owned AI company that connects AI to the firm's knowledge and workflows for client service. Its practice pages also describe a concrete AI workflow: drafting a bespoke S-1 in minutes and updating it as terms change with a few prompts. The disclosure is thin and promotional. It does not name the S-1 tool, explain how it works, or publish any AI-use or client-data policy, so whether it goes beyond a marketing mention is only partly established. Missing for 10: a published AI-use or governance policy, named and documented tools with specifics on how they are used in matters, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the firm publishes how it uses AI in client service — named tools, policies, or AI-practice products of its own — beyond a marketing mention

citations.quote: Cooley AI – a firm-owned artificial intelligence company. By connecting AI to the firm's knowledge, workflows and human judgment, Cooley AI enables our lawyers to provide clients with faster insights, greater value and a smoother experience.
Complete an initial, bespoke S-1 draft in minutes rather than days, accelerating the path to substantive legal work
Update the S-1 as transaction terms change – all with a few simple prompts.
